summary: The discussion proposes a semantic contract between applications and networks to enable differentiated treatment of AI traffic based on factors like urgency and data type. This approach utilizes an internal network intelligence component called IntelliNode to combine semantic inputs with real-time network states, allowing for microsecond-level decisions on routing, buffering, and device selection. Future plans involve refining the contract model, defining header extensions for line-rate processing, clarifying decision boundaries, and building prototypes to validate performance improvements for AI workloads.
